text:
anya: alerting — since 22:05 UTC ap-south1 has a slow burn of tiny-pod evictions. pending-tiny-pods up 60 -> 330 in ~40m, attach timeouts surfacing. fragmentation map shows lots of 0.25/0.5 GPU islands.

mike: ugh. any node logs showing nf_conntrack or attach service errors?

jules: pasted from ap-south1-nv-09 at 22:12:
```
Jul 19 22:12:03 kubelet[4021]: attach: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = websocket: close 1006
Jul 19 22:12:04 kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
Jul 19 22:12:05 kubelet[4021]: attach: timeout waiting for device attach: context deadline exceeded
Jul 19 22:12:05 kubelet[4021]: evicting pod tiny-eval-2a due to attach timeout
```

samir: looks like the usual combo: conntrack exhaustion + scheduler-driven scatter (rack-awareness). Warm-pool attaches are hammering the attach-service sockets.

infra-bot: [alert] ap-south1: tiny-evict-rate > 50/min for 20m (alert_id: infra:tiny-evict:3724).

ops-lead: mitigations: 1) throttle warm-pool attach concurrency 2) add small scheduler soft-hint to prefer co-location of tiny pods 3) consider per-node conntrack bump on a tiny canary only if controller changes fail.

anya: prefer controller + scheduler changes first. bumping kernel knobs fleet-wide is risky. we should also add tiny jitter on attach attempts (random 30-200ms) to avoid synchronized bursts.

mike: i'll patch warm-pool controller to support ATTACH_LIMIT=6/s and jitter=30-200ms and canary-deploy to ap-south1-a.

jules: i'll add a scheduler scoring rule: if pod.request.gpu <= 0.5 and node.tiny_count > 0 then +90 score. respects tenant anti-affinity. PR coming.

samir: two quick notes: 1) coalescing reduces attach ops but increases CPU density on packed hosts; watch CPU steal and oom events. 2) instrument "attach_ops_saved" metric so we can quantify rollback impact.

ops-lead: canary plan: 1) deploy controller attach limiter to ap-south1-a at 22:50 UTC 2) enable scheduler coalesce on 8 canary nodes (label canary=tiny-pack) 3) monitor 30m (attach-p95, evict-rate, pending-tiny-pods, nf_conntrack_count) 4) rollback if evict-rate > 12/min or attach-p95 > 30s. tag nodes for quick revert.

infra-bot: [update] canary started 22:52 UTC.

mike: initial canary metrics after 6m: pending-tiny-pods -25%, evict-rate -29%, attach-p95 down from 41s to 17s.

anya: promising. i'll watch node conntrack memory and slab. if we see slab growth or oom_killer, revert conntrack bump.

jules: reminder: make the scheduler hint opt-in per-namespace. noisy tenants should be able to opt for spread. we should also add a per-tenant override metric.

ops-lead: good. follow-ups: 1) rollout gradually if canary stable, 2) add attach proxy RFC (long-term) to avoid websocket churn, 3) document runbook steps.

infra-bot: [final] canary window closed 23:22 UTC: evict-rate=6.8/min (target <10), attach-p95=19.4s (target <25s), pending-tiny-pods stabilized. recommending gradual rollout with per-namespace opt-in.

anya: filing incident notes and PR links now. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
